quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue while driving. You are too tired to drive safely if you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or turn up the radio to stay awake. If you notice these signs, park in a safe place and take a short nap to refresh yourself.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
To stop the seat belt warning light or buzzer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: Should you use high beam headlights in fog, snow, and heavy rain?
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, and heavy rain. High beam light reflects off precipitation and creates glare that makes it harder to see.

questions.question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are jaywalking or crossing where they should not. Always stop for them.

questions.question: What happens to fines for traffic violations in school zones?
questions.explanation: In Maine, fines for traffic violations are doubled in school zones. Drive carefully when going through a school zone.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Adjust your speed to safely complete the turn.

questions.question: What should you do if you become tired while driving?

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If you become tired while driving, stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, making driving unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must and must not do. This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign tells you to prepare to allow traffic to safely merge from the right.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area where road construction workers work.
The area where people can cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where people can cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are marked with white lines to show where people should cross. Some crosswalks have lines between or instead of the outer lines. Crosswalks can also be unmarked.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals, should a driver slow down, look, and listen?
questions.explanation: At railroad crossings without warning devices or with only a crossbuck sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains or railroad equipment. Only cross if it is safe.

questions.question: Do safety belts help you stay alert by keeping you from slouching while you drive?
questions.explanation: Safety belts keep you upright and alert. They also reduce fatigue by helping your body stay in the seat when the car bounces or turns.

questions.question: When can you drive in a lane with a red X signal above it?

options.text: When there is no oncoming traffic.
When you are passing the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed throughout the day. They also show if toll booths are open. Never drive in a lane marked with a red X.

questions.question: When can you park directly across from a fire station entrance?

options.text: If emergency vehicles just left the station

questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire station driveway or directly across from the entrance.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic laws as if there were no construction.

questions.explanation: Always slow down and follow directions from flaggers or police in construction zones. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right, what should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your car between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: What risk does fatigue increase?

options.text: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes poor decisions about speed and distance. It increases crash risk and slows your reaction time. You could fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting yourself or others.

questions.question: What does alcohol do?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that slows your brain. It reduces the skills you need for safe driving. It slows reaction time and impairs judgment.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: An aggressive driver is driving behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact. Speeding up or blocking them will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: You miss your exit on an interstate highway. What should you do?

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back.
Roll down your window and ask another driver for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on a highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: In a car with airbags, where should children age 12 and under sit?

options.text: The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags are dangerous for children. Anyone age 12 or under should sit in the back seat.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are approaching.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers that bicycles may be crossing.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert and keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis. Do not stare at one thing for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and help guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: While backing out of your driveway.

questions.explanation: Adjust all mirrors before starting your engine so you do not have to lean forward or backward. You will not have time to adjust them when driving in traffic.

questions.question: When taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about the effects before driving.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about the effects before driving.
questions.explanation: Medicine can affect your ability to drive. Ask your doctor or pharmacist how any medication will affect your driving.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off the water or moisture and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal your intentions, even when no other traffic is visible.
Signal only if other traffic is visible.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intentions, even when no other traffic is visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from the curb. Do not skip this step—it is the law and keeps everyone safe.

questions.question: Motor vehicle drivers should give extra space to children on bicycles because:

options.text: Children do not have the same reflexes as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see than adults.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware that children on bikes may come onto the road unexpectedly from the sidewalk.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as possible.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, stay far away from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance. Never tailgate.

questions.question: The fatal accident rate for night driving is nearly three times greater than for daytime driving.
questions.explanation: Fatal accidents at night are nearly three times more common than during the day, even though fewer miles are driven at night. Drive slower at night because visibility is much worse in the dark.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Drive carefully on wet roads.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means drivers should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge in.
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign means two lanes going the same direction will soon merge into one lane. Be ready to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge into your lane.

questions.question: You should use your horn:

options.text: Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
To get other drivers moving in traffic.
When you're angry with another driver.
To say hello to another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Other drivers cannot see you unless they are looking your way. Use your horn to get their attention and prevent a collision.

questions.question: Driving ability can be impaired by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires the driver to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness all affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells you that the divided highway is about to end.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It makes you feel more confident than you should be.

questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and affects your judgment and balance. It makes you feel overly confident. Alcohol also reduces your vision and ability to judge distance, making it hard to react to what's around you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you to drive carefully when the road is wet and slippery.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Don't worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: A traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.explanation: You must obey a police officer's directions, even if they go against traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Make sure the lane is clear before you move into it.

questions.question: Before driving through an intersection, you should look:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection. Watch for pedestrians, other vehicles, and hazards.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and others.
Don't drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you can't see as well. Take steps to make night driving safer for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you can stop only to:

options.text: Park for less than five minutes.

questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: If a driver gets ____ points in one year, their license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: If a driver gets 12 or more points within 12 months, their license will be suspended.

questions.question: You should remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: Remove snow, ice, and frost from all windows, headlights, and taillights before driving. You need to see clearly, and other drivers need to see your vehicle.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times while driving.

questions.question: Before moving back to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your original lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Know that the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.

questions.explanation: Give a distracted driver extra space. A driver who is not paying full attention is more likely to cause an accident. Do not copy their unsafe behavior.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let another driver take over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let another driver take over.
questions.explanation: Stop driving when you feel tired. Take breaks every hour on long trips. Share driving with another person so you both can rest.

questions.question: If you have the right-of-way at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will follow the rules.
Check for traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists before moving forward.
Wave other drivers ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists before moving forward.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left, then right, then left again. Check for other traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Always yield if it prevents a collision.

questions.question: Posters, signs, and window decals on windshields and windows:

options.text: Are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.
Are allowed if they allow some visibility.
Are prohibited unless the law requires them.
Are allowed if they do not have offensive language.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are prohibited unless the law requires them.
questions.explanation: No signs, posters, or stickers can be placed on vehicle windows, unless the law specifically requires them.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Right turns are allowed on a red light.

questions.explanation: This sign means no right turns are permitted at this intersection.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Stare directly ahead at the road.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind their car.
questions.explanation: Watch everything around your vehicle—to the sides, ahead, and behind. This helps you notice hazards and stay safe.
